reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address Q235 steel, its oxidation behavior under controlled oxygen partial pressures, or its performance in high-temperature salt environments. E1 discusses oxide film formation on Nb alloys, and E2 describes electrodeposited protective films on metal electrodes in room-temperature NaCl solution. Neither passage provides support for the key premises about oxide scale formation, adhesion, or corrosion protection on Q235 steel under the proposed conditions.
premises: High oxygen partial pressure during annealing produces a dense, well-adherent oxide scale on Q235 steel.
A dense, well-adherent oxide scale limits outward Fe diffusion and inward salt ion penetration at high temperature.
Low oxygen partial pressure during annealing produces a porous or defective oxide scale.
A porous/defective oxide scale is more susceptible to cracking, spallation, and accelerated corrosion under salt exposure.
The protective mechanism is activated under high-temperature kinetics (700–900 °C) and not at room temperature.
